tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: Thank you for your willingness to participate. Today I'd like to ask you some questions about your experiences with commuting. First, what kinds of places do you usually go to during the week and how do you get there?
tasks.sample: During the week, I mostly go to three places: my university, the library, and a gym near my apartment. I take the subway to university because it’s cheap and usually on time. The ride takes about 25 minutes. The library is close to campus, so I just walk there after class. As for the gym, I go by bike. It’s only ten minutes away, and it also gives me a little workout before I actually start exercising. So, subway for longer trips, walking for medium ones, and biking for short trips.
tasks.analysis: 中文：感谢你愿意参与。今天我想问你一些关于你通勤体验的问题。首先，你平时一周通常会去哪些地方？你是怎么去这些地方的？
tasks.title: Interview

tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: Got it. Can you describe how someone in your family or a friend usually travels to work or school? How much time does it take and what transportation does the person use?
tasks.sample: I’ll talk about my best friend. She works at a marketing company downtown. Every morning, she takes the bus to the train station, then rides the train for about 30 minutes, and finally walks ten minutes from the station to her office. The whole trip takes around an hour each way. She says the worst part is when the bus is late and she barely catches the train. Sometimes she listens to podcasts or reads on the train to make the time useful. For her, commuting is tiring, but she doesn't have a better option.
tasks.analysis: 中文：明白了。你能描述一下你家里或你的一位朋友通常是如何去上班或上学的吗？那个人通常花多长时间、使用什么交通工具？
tasks.title: Interview

tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: OK thanks. Next question. Some people believe that living close to work or school improves quality of life, while others think location doesn't matter much. What do you think and why?
tasks.sample: Yes, I strongly believe living close to work or school really improves quality of life. First, you save a huge amount of time. If you commute two hours every day, that’s ten hours a week — time you could use for sleeping, cooking healthy meals, or hanging out with friends. Second, a short commute means less daily stress. You don’t have to deal with traffic jams, packed subways, or running late all the time. You arrive calmer and more focused. In the long run, a shorter commute gives you better mental and physical health. So location absolutely matters.
tasks.analysis: 中文：好的，谢谢。下一个问题。有些人认为，住在离工作或学校近的地方可以提高生活质量，而另一些人则认为地点并不那么重要。你怎么看？为什么？
tasks.title: Interview

tasks.instruction: Listen to the question, then respond.
tasks.stem: Great. Final question. Some people believe that employers should reimburse employees for their commuting costs, while others think that employees should pay for their own travel to work. Which view do you agree with and why?
tasks.sample: I agree that employers should reimburse commuting costs, at least partially. Here’s why. First, commuting is required for most jobs. You can’t do the work if you can’t get there, so it’s more like a work-related expense than a personal one. Second, it’s about fairness. People often live far away because housing near the office is too expensive. Why should they pay more just because their salary doesn’t cover high rent? Paying for commuting also shows that a company values its employees’ time and money. In the end, it’s a smart way to improve job satisfaction.
tasks.analysis: 中文：很好。最后一个问题。有些人认为雇主应该报销员工的通勤费用，而另一些人则认为员工应该自己承担上班的交通费用。你同意哪种观点？为什么？
tasks.title: Interview
